hints: Recall that the graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ is the reflection of $y = f(x)$ in the line $y=x$.
Reflect the branch in the second quadrant ($x<0, y>4$) across $y=x$ into the fourth quadrant ($x>4, y<0$).
Draw and label the line of symmetry $y=x$ with the reflected curve.
walkthrough:
Identify key graphical features of $f(x) = \frac{2}{x^2}+4$ for $x < 0$:
$$\text{Domain: } x < 0, \quad \text{Range: } y > 4$$
$$\text{Vertical asymptote: } x = 0, \quad \text{Horizontal asymptote: } y = 4$$

Determine the corresponding features of the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$ by swapping $x$ and $y$:
$$\text{Domain: } x > 4, \quad \text{Range: } y < 0$$
$$\text{Vertical asymptote: } x = 4, \quad \text{Horizontal asymptote: } y = 0$$
Sketch the mirror line $y = x$ as a dashed diagonal and draw the reflected inverse curve in the fourth quadrant ($x > 4, y < 0$).

hints: Take the square root, choosing the negative sign because the original domain is $x < 0$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = f(x)$ and swap variables to form the inverse equation:
$$x = \frac{2}{y^2} + 4$$

Rearrange to make $y^2$ the subject:
$$x - 4 = \frac{2}{y^2} \implies y^2 = \frac{2}{x-4}$$

Take the square root and choose the negative branch since the original domain is $x < 0$:
$$y = -\sqrt{\frac{2}{x-4}}$$
$$f^{-1}(x) = -\sqrt{\frac{2}{x-4}} \quad (\text{for } x > 4)$$

Select the negative root since the domain of $f$ is $x < 0$:
$$x = -2$$

hints: Consider the ranges/signs of the outputs of $f(x)$ and $f^{-1}(x)$.
Note that $f(x) > 4 > 0$ for all $x < 0$, whereas $f^{-1}(x) < 0$ for all $x > 4$.
walkthrough:
State the range of $f(x)$ and the range of $f^{-1}(x)$:
$$\text{Range of } f: f(x) > 4 > 0 \quad (\text{outputs are strictly positive})$$
$$\text{Range of } f^{-1}: f^{-1}(x) < 0 \quad (\text{outputs are strictly negative})$$

Conclude why they cannot intersect:
$$\text{Since } f(x) > 0 \text{ and } f^{-1}(x) < 0 \text{ for all defined values, their outputs can never be equal, so } f^{-1}(x) = f(x) \text{ has no solution.}$$
